chunks: A man said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, do not be angry with me.” He said, “Why?” He said, “Because of what I wish to ask you about.” He said, “Speak.” He said, “And you will not be angry?” He said, “And I will not be angry.” He said, “What do you say about your statement concerning Laylat al-Qadr and the descent of the angels and the Spirit in it to the Awṣiyāʾ? Do they come to them with a matter that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had not known, or do they come to them with a matter that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله knew? And I have known that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله died while none of his knowledge existed except that ʿAlī عليه السلام was preserving it.”

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said, “What is there between me and you, O man? And who brought you to me?” He said, “Al-Qaḍāʾ brought me to you in seeking the religion.” He said, “Then understand what I say to you: when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken on the night journey, he did not descend until Allah, Majestic is His mention, taught him the knowledge of what had been and what will be. Much of that knowledge was in summary form, and its explanation would come in Laylat al-Qadr. Likewise, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام had known the totalities of knowledge, and its explanation would come in the nights of al-Qadr just as it had been with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

The questioner said, “Was there not explanation within those totalities?” He said, “Yes, but the command from Allah the Exalted only comes in the nights of al-Qadr to the Prophet and to the Awṣiyāʾ: ‘Do such and such,’ regarding a matter they had already known; they were commanded how to act concerning it.” I said, “Explain this to me.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not die except while preserving the totality of the knowledge and its explanation.”

I said, “So that which used to come to him in the nights of al-Qadr, what knowledge was it?” He said, “The command and the facilitation concerning what he had already known.” The questioner said, “Then does knowledge occur for them in the nights of al-Qadr besides what they knew?” He said, “This is among what they were commanded to conceal, and none knows the explanation of what you asked about except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
The questioner said, “Do the Awṣiyāʾ know what the prophets do not know?” He said, “No. And how could a Waṣī know other than the knowledge of that which was entrusted to him?”

The questioner said, “Do we have room to say that one of the successors knows what another does not know?” He said, “No. No prophet dies except that his knowledge is within his successor. The angels and the Spirit only descend in Laylat al-Qadr with the judgment by which he judges among the servants.”

The questioner said, “And had they known that judgment?” He said, “Yes, they had known it, but they are not able to execute any part of it until they are commanded in the nights of al-Qadr how they are to act until the coming year.”
The questioner said, “O Abū Jaʿfar, I am not able to deny this.” Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said, “Whoever denies it is not from us.”

The questioner said, “O Abū Jaʿfar, what about the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله—did something come to him in the nights of al-Qadr that he had not known?” He said, “It is not permissible for you to ask about this. As for the knowledge of what had been and what will be, no prophet and no successor dies except that the successor after him knows it. As for this knowledge that you ask about, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused to disclose it to the Awṣiyāʾ except to themselves.”

The questioner said, “O son of the Messenger of Allah, how may I know that Laylat al-Qadr occurs in every year?” He said, “When the month of Ramaḍān comes, then recite Sūrat al-Dukhān every night one hundred times. Then when the night of the twenty-third arrives, you will behold the confirmation of what you asked about.”

key_terms.الرُّوحِ: The Spirit descending along with the angels in Laylat al-Qadr.
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The divinely designated successors entrusted with inherited sacred knowledge.
key_terms.الْحُكْمِ: The judgment or ruling by which the Imam judges among people.
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: Divine ordainment that led the questioner to seek the religion.
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةِ: The angels who descend with divine command.
key_terms.جُمَلَ الْعِلْمِ: The total or summary form of knowledge held prior to detailed explanation.
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the night in which divine command and detailed decrees are conveyed.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Laylat al-Qadr, the descent of the angels, and the knowledge of the Awṣiyāʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Awṣiyāʾ possess the totality of divinely granted knowledge, while in Laylat al-Qadr the detailed command and mode of implementation are conveyed to them. It also affirms the continuity of knowledge from each prophet or Waṣī to the one after him, and connects the descent of the angels and the Spirit with divine judgment and yearly command.
